title: Analytical corpus case (one JSONL line)
description: One case of the analytical corpus for ARCH-ANALYTICAL-RELATION-001. A case is an observation the engine must judge: an asserted derivation or projection over a typed relation, the verdict the doctrine expects, and either the causal diagnostic (illegal) or the missing premise (unproven). Case identity and diagnostic identity are separate on purpose: several cases may share one diagnostic, so the count of distinct diagnostics an engine emits is a property of its causal partitioning, not of how many rows were authored. `stage` is the earliest construction stage whose facts decide the case; an engine built to stage N is judged only on cases with stage <= N. `evidence` says whether the relation type alone decides it (schema) or actual rows are needed (instance). Shape only is enforced here; term resolution, form-name leaks, engine coverage, bijection, source citation, and doctrine drift are checked by packages/ds-codegen/src/analytical/corpus-integrity.ts.

case.description: Identity of the observation. Unique within the corpus. Independent of any diagnostic name.

verdict.description: What a correct engine returns for this case. A legal corpus is a separate file. `unproven` is the third judgment: the admissible set narrows on a missing premise instead of blocking or silently passing.

diagnostic.description: Required when verdict is illegal. The causal diagnostic the engine emits; must be a row of the doctrine's diagnostic catalogue. Many cases may share one diagnostic.

obligation.description: Required when verdict is unproven. The missing premise, as a vocabulary term, carried forward as an obligation the runtime or the author must discharge.

engine.description: The checkability engine that adjudicates. Must equal vocabulary.json `engines` (drift-gated).

stage.description: Earliest construction stage (doctrine 'Order of construction') whose facts decide this case: 1 = L0-L2 field algebra, grain, aggregability; 2 = L3 view algebra; 3 = L3.5 task and L4 projection/combinators; 4 = realization; 5 = accessibility projections; 6 = cross-substrate.

evidence.description: schema: decidable from the relation type alone. instance: needs actual rows (values, null kinds, edge weights).

asserted.description: The derivation or projection being asserted, in L0-L4 vocabulary. Never a form name.

cause.description: For illegal: the fact that makes the assertion ill-typed. For unproven: the premise that is missing. Never a form name. Prose; the mechanical claim is only that `terms` resolve.

terms.description: The namespaced vocabulary references the case declares (namespace:term). Every one must resolve in vocabulary.json. This proves the declared references resolve; it does not prove the prose is exhausted by them.

colloquial.description: What a practitioner would call this. Exempt from the form-name denylist; exists to show the name is downstream of the cause.

source.description: External standards that license this case's obligation. The obligation is semantic and belongs to the relation; the standard is EVIDENCE that the obligation is real and not self-authored. Citing a standard here never admits its vocabulary into the analytical relation — no aria/role/html term may appear in `terms`. Required by corpus-integrity for any case declaring a `projection:` term (CORPUS_SOURCE_UNCITED); optional otherwise, because most cases are licensed by measurement theory rather than by a published standard.

standard.description: wcag: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines success criteria. aria: the WAI-ARIA specification. apg: the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide.

status.description: normative: the citation is a requirement of a W3C Recommendation (a WCAG success criterion, an ARIA attribute definition). guidance: it is advisory (APG is explicitly non-normative and can itself recommend patterns that override otherwise-correct semantics). A guidance-only obligation is weaker evidence and is recorded as such rather than excluded.

ref.description: The citation as a reader would look it up, e.g. 'WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships' or 'APG Table Pattern'.
